20                 THE SECRETARY:   Resolution 2314, by 

21    Senator Ramos, recognizing the New York Chapter 

22    of the National Domestic Workers Alliance.

23                 ACTING PRESIDENT BAILEY:   Senator 

24    Ramos on the resolution.

25                 SENATOR RAMOS:   Yes, thank you, 


                                                                7495

 1    Mr. President.  

 2                 Today we recognize the New York 

 3    State Chapter of the National Domestic Workers 

 4    Alliance and the extraordinary workers that they 

 5    represent.  

 6                 When we talk about what makes 

 7    New York work, we often talk about industries and 

 8    businesses and institutions.  But behind all of 

 9    those things are people who make it possible for 

10    everyone else to show up:  The nanny who cares 

11    for a child before going to school, the home care 

12    worker helping a senior age with dignity, the 

13    house cleaner whose labor gives a family time and 

14    stability.  Domestic workers are the workers who 

15    make all other work possible.

16                 And yet for generations they were 

17    excluded from basic labor protections that many 

18    other workers have taken for granted.  And that 

19    exclusion wasn't accidental.  Much of this work 

20    has historically been performed by women, by 

21    immigrants, Black women and women of color.  And 

22    for too long society depended on their labor 

23    while denying them the dignity, recognition, pay 

24    and protections they deserve.

25                 But domestic workers are organized.  


                                                                7496

 1    They refuse to remain invisible.  And so today we 

 2    honor that legacy of pioneers like Dorothy 

 3    Bolden, who understood that dignity is not 

 4    something workers should have to ask for; it's 

 5    something that they are owed.

 6                 The National Domestic Workers 

 7    Alliance has carried that legacy, organizing 

 8    workers, developing leaders, recovering stolen 

 9    wages, and fighting for policies that recognize 

10    the value of care work.  Because care work -- 

11    because care is work, and care workers deserve 

12    rights.  

13                 Their advocacy has helped secure 

14    paid sick leave, paid family leave, workplace 

15    protections, and greater recognition of the 

16    essential role domestic workers play in our 

17    economy and in our communities.

18                 As chair of the Senate Labor 

19    Committee, I believe protecting workers means 

20    protecting all workers -- not just the workers 

21    whose jobs are highly visible, not just the 

22    workers with the loudest voices, all workers.

23                 And few workers embody the values of 

24    service, sacrifice and care more than domestic 

25    workers.  They care for our children, our 


                                                                7497

 1    parents, and our homes.  And in doing so, they 

 2    hold our communities together.

 3                 Today we proudly recognize the 

 4    New York Chapter of the National Domestic Workers 

 5    Alliance for their leadership, their advocacy, 

 6    and their unwavering commitment to dignity, 

 7    fairness and justice for working people.  

 8                 Mr. President, one of the most 

 9    incredible labor organizers from my community, 

10    Avi Gayil {ph}, is here with all of the domestic 

11    workers from across New York State who are making 

12    change happen.  Please extend all of the 

13    courtesies of the house to them.

14                 Thank you.

15                 ACTING PRESIDENT BAILEY:   Thank 

16    you, Senator Ramos.

17                 Senator Hinchey on the resolution.

18                 SENATOR HINCHEY:   Thank you, 

19    Mr. President.

20                 I rise today with profound gratitude 

21    to honor an extraordinary movement and the 

22    remarkable women who have built it.  And I want 

23    to thank the sponsor for this resolution.

24                 For the past decade, the We Dream in 

25    Black New York Chapter has been rewriting the 


                                                                7498

 1    story of what's possible when people refuse to 

 2    accept injustice.  Today, as we celebrate their 

 3    10-year anniversary, I want the Senate record to 

 4    reflect something our nation needs to hear.  The 

 5    domestic workers of this country are among the 

 6    most powerful leaders and change-makers that we 

 7    have.  

 8                 I was meeting with my sisters from 

 9    the Red Carpet for Social Justice Coalition, many 

10    of whom are members of We Dream in Black.  After 

11    they told me about this incredible milestone, I 

12    knew that when the day came for us to welcome 

13    them here to the Capitol, I had to take a moment 

14    to say thank you, because across our communities 

15    they are the unsung heroes whose leadership 

16    deserves to be enshrined in the Senate record.  

17                 Labor is the backbone of every 

18    community, and domestic workers do some of the 

19    most important, sacred, difficult and deeply 

20    personal work there is.  They are the people 

21    nurturing our children with patience and 

22    tenderness.  They are the people caring for our 

23    aging loved ones with dignity and gentleness.  

24    And they often become trusted members of our 

25    families.  


                                                                7499

 1                 They deserve to be seen and 

 2    celebrated.  Their work requires tremendous skill 

 3    and emotional intelligence.  And without their 

 4    caring hands and generous hearts, so much would 

 5    fall away.  

 6                 For far too long, their labor has 

 7    been overlooked and underprotected, from the 

 8    exclusion of domestic workers from Social 

 9    Security in 1935 to the challenges and inequities 

10    still today.  

11                 But We Dream in Black has been 

12    changing that reality.  In just 10 years they 

13    have built a home for Black, Afro-Latina and 

14    Afro-descendant domestic workers to unite, 

15    amplify their voices and illuminate their 

16    collective power.  

17                 They've recovered more than half a  

18    million dollars in stolen wages, helped workers 

19    understand their rights, and as the sponsor said, 

20    they've won landmark victories for paid family 

21    leave and paid sick and safe leave.  

22                 This is what the labor movement 

23    looks like.  It's ordinary people standing 

24    together, lifting each other up, and moving 

25    mountains that once seemed unmovable.  It's women 


                                                                7500

 1    refusing to accept anything less than the rights 

 2    and fairness that they so fundamentally deserve.

 3                 What We Dream in Black has achieved 

 4    over the last 10 years is nothing short of 

 5    remarkable.  They have built a movement with a 

 6    capital "M."  And they have inspired so many to 

 7    lead with courage, compassion, and belief in 

 8    themselves.

 9                 To the phenomenal members of 

10    We Dream in Black here in the chamber today, we 

11    see you, we celebrate you, we thank you for being 

12    innovators, problem solvers, and for raising your 

13    voices to raise labor standards for domestic 

14    workers.  Your fight is our fight.  Happy 10-year 

15    anniversary.

16                 Thank you, Mr. President.  I proudly 

17    vote aye.

18                 ACTING PRESIDENT BAILEY:   Thank 

19    you, Senator Hinchey.  

20                 Senator Sanders on the resolution.

21                 SENATOR SANDERS:   Thank you, 

22    Mr. President.  

23                 I too want to commend the sponsor 

24    for this move.  I would be -- it wouldn't be 

25    right if I didn't stand up for this moment.  


                                                                7501

 1                 I am the son of a domestic worker, 

 2    and my mother actually had the ability to go out 

 3    and work and help raise other families and then 

 4    come back and raise her own family.  She had that 

 5    much love.  

 6                 So I commend all of the people who 

 7    are able to get out there and share love in this 

 8    day and age, a love that this society desperately 

 9    needs.  So I continue to urge you to be the best 

10    you and then to come home and to make sure that 

11    your children have everything that they need.  

12                 I commend the struggle that you're 

13    having or that you're doing and stand shoulder to 

14    shoulder with you to make sure that you are 

15    treated with the dignity that you deserve.

16                 I proudly vote aye.

17                 ACTING PRESIDENT BAILEY:   Thank 

18    you, Senator Sanders.

20    sheroes, the fabric of society, the domestic 

21    workers, we celebrate you and we thank you for 

22    coming to the Capitol.  

23                 We recognize you, and on behalf of 

24    the Senate we extend to you all of the privileges 

25    and cordialities of the house.

 5                 SENATOR SEPÚLVEDA:   Thank you, 

 6    Mr. President, for allowing me to speak on this 

 7    nomination.  

 8                 But before I do, I just want to take 

 9    a personal point of privilege and thank retiring 

10    Justice Richard Sise, who has been just an 

11    incredible leader of the Court of Claims for 

12    several years, and he's going to be sorely 

13    missed.

14                 After much deliberation and 

15    commitment and all of the work by all of the 

16    nominees, I am proud to announce that today we 

17    will bring to the floor the nomination of four 

18    interim Supreme Court justices, seven new Court

20    extended.  

21                 Each and every person who appeared 

22    before our Judiciary Committee, every candidate, 

23    has an incredible story and an incredible resume.  

24    And I am so proud that this is my first nominees 

25    as the new chair of the Judiciary Committee, and 


                                                                7507

 1    I am so proud that each and every one of them

 1    as a whole.  Yesterday during the nominating

 1                 Construction workers understand that

 8    dressed, travels to the job site, arranges

10    the job has been canceled because of the weather 

11    or some other reason beyond their control -- and

13    kept their commitment, and the employer faced no 

14    consequence.

16    bill establishes that when workers show up ready 

17    to work, their time is valued.  If a construction 

18    worker reports to a job site and is sent home 

19    without cause, they should be compensated at 

20    least for some of their time.  And if a shift is 

21    canceled with little notice, workers should not 

22    bear the full cost of that decision.

24    deserve more than our gratitude, they deserve 

25    predictability and respect.  Their time is

 1    Mr. President.

 2                 2026 marks 10 years since 

 3    India Cummings died while in custody at the 

 4    Erie County sheriff's office.  

 5                 India was born and raised in 

 6    Rochester.  Later in life, she and her mother 

 7    moved to my district, where she lived in the City 

 8    of Lackawanna.  

 9                 I started my legislative career 

10    about two years after India's death.  But the 

11    aftermath of the situation engulfed my early 

12    years as an elected official.  Six months 

13    after I took my oath of office as a county 

14    legislator, the State Commission on Corrections 

15    determined India's death was a homicide due to 

16    neglect.  

17                 She was not eating, she was not 

18    drinking, she was living in extremely unsanitary 

19    conditions, and she had an untreated broken arm.  

20    Her mental health severely deteriorated in jail.  

21    And despite two different judges ordering her to 

22    undergo a psychiatric evaluation, she did not 

23    receive one before her untimely death.

24                 This bill before us seeks to remedy 

25    two points that I believe could have saved 


                                                                7565

 1    India's life.  One, timely transfer to a mental 

 2    health facility.  And two, early intervention for 

 3    a family member.

 4                 This bill requires the process for a 

 5    mental health evaluation to start within 48 hours 

 6    of a mental health crisis.  India sat in the 

 7    Erie County holding center for two weeks without 

 8    any mental health intervention.  

 9                 I have spoken with India's mother a 

10    number of times over the years, and she truly 

11    believed that if she, as a mother, was allowed to 

12    speak or knew what was happening with her 

13    daughter, she could have helped prevent her 

14    baby's death.

15                 India's death was a primary 

16    motivator for this legislative action as I took 

17    my seat as a county legislator.  It led to many 

18    things in county government in Erie County.  It 

19    led to me bringing body cameras and a blind-spot 

20    camera into Erie County jails.  It led to the 

21    creation of the Erie County Corrections 

22    Specialist Advisory Board.  And it led to the 

23    creation of a medically assisted treatment 

24    program in Erie County jails.  

25                 But these improvements did not 


                                                                7566

 1    directly address the causes of India's death.  I
